open_questions: Accelera unit economics and separate option sizing not in base proof.
Reinvestment rate and incremental return on capital use versioned bounds pending segment capital bridge.
Insider net selling vs planned sale programs not fully parsed from Form 4 footnotes.
thesis: Cummins Inc. (NYSE: CMI) designs, manufactures, and services diesel and natural-gas engines, generator sets, and related components for on-highway trucks, construction, mining, marine, and power-generation markets. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$33.67 billion** and operating income was **$4.03 billion**. **[Fact]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$3.62 billion** and capital spending was **$1.24 billion**, leaving **$2.39 billion** of normalized owner earnings. **[Fact]** Reportable segments include Engine, Distribution, Components, Power Systems, and Accelera (zero-emissions technologies). **[Inference]** Cummins is a global industrial compounder with cyclical end markets, a large installed base that supports aftermarket revenue, and a strategic pivot toward hydrogen, battery, and fuel-cell products through Accelera.
why_market_wrong: The market may be capitalizing **engine franchise durability and decarbonization optionality** while underweighting **$7.7 billion of debt** on the March 2026 balance sheet and **capital spending near $1.2 billion per year** that already reduces owner cash below reported operating cash flow. **[Inference]** At **$635.96**, the stock trades at roughly **2.3 times** our base proof value per share after refreshing debt from filings, implying the market expects reinvestment returns and terminal economics well above our bounded base case. Insider activity shows large net sales versus modest open-market buys over the past year, which weakens the "insiders know more" bull case unless those sales are largely planned 10b5-1 programs.
